scope: Film Programme homepage, desktop and mobile comparison board
prompt: Create a high-fidelity UX/UI DESIGN COMPARISON BOARD for Cinema Platform, a Ukrainian cinema website. This is an actual interface mockup, not a moodboard or poster, not code. Landscape board approximately 1800 by 1200. On the left show a large straight-on desktop homepage viewport with readable real interface regions (about 1240 by 930 at scale); on the right show a fully independent, correctly reflowed mobile homepage viewport (about 390 by 930 at scale), not a shrunken desktop. No perspective devices or computer props. Small neutral board label above each: Desktop, Mobile. BOTH views show the same Film Programme UX: visible navigation, film imagery and title, date context, clearly readable screening buttons directly beside/below that film, and the start of a second film entry below. Film-first editorial discovery, with integrated showtimes, never a uniform repeated card grid. Desktop and mobile opening viewport must include at least one usable-looking screening action without scrolling. Actual brand text "Cinema Platform". Ukrainian navigation "Фільми", "Розклад", "Квитки"; secondary "Увійти". Date "26 жовтня" and next-date choice "27 жовтня". Demo programme lead title "Дюна: Частина друга", secondary title "Памфір", third if space "Тіні забутих предків". Programme imagery: rich illustrative cinematic desert scene with a small cloaked figure, second film a photographic-looking rural Ukrainian forest scene. Imagery is illustrative not actual licensed movie stills. Lead screenings: "18:30 · Зал 1", "20:45 · Зал 2"; secondary "19:10 · Зал 1". Include small action "Усі сеанси". No prices, seat counts, availability guarantees, age ratings, screening formats, premiere dates, reviews, star ratings, recommendation claims, marketing statistics, or countdowns. Add a legible small footer outside both viewports: "Концепт · демонстраційна програма". Same content in both views. Exquisite polished typography and aligned meaningful controls; clear visual distinction between headings, metadata and actions. Keep text on solid contrasting surfaces, touch-sized mobile controls; text is not embedded illegibly over busy imagery. No decorative icon tiles, stock SaaS sections, glass panels, rounded card grid, gratuitous gradients or meaningless ornaments. Image must communicate actual homepage composition at finished visual fidelity. DIRECTION C — VELVET INTERVAL. An intimate, contemporary cinema identity built from aubergine, peach and photographic light; cinematic and sophisticated without resembling a streaming-service dashboard. Solid deep wine/aubergine #2A1B2B canvas, warm pale peach #F4DDD1 primary text, muted mauve #C8B6C7 secondary text, pale peach solid programme-action surfaces with dark plum text. No black/red, neon, decorative gradients, glassmorphism, rounded card carousels or luxury gold. Typography: fluid expressive italic Cyrillic editorial serif titles (PT Serif italic character) juxtaposed with a clear modern sans for times and navigation, no unreadable script. Desktop: quiet widely spaced masthead on plum; explicit Films/Schedule/Tickets navigation with restrained peach underline. Below, an intimate cinematic DIPTYCH: a striking tall crop of the desert film image on left roughly 45%, generous plum negative space on right with huge elegant two-line title and a short readable sentence. Title stays off the busy photo. Under that copy, a broad pale-peach booking band has visible date choices and two dark-text showtime actions with hall labels, so image atmosphere and usable programme are contiguous. A smaller secondary film preview enters below as a horizontal photographic crop plus type, separated with a thin mauve rule. Composition deliberately uses an off-center image and expansive typographic pause; no full-bleed background image. Mobile: simpler masthead with visible ticket access; date remains visible above film; title before a carefully cropped image only around 190 CSS pixels tall, then pale-peach showtime band with readable actions and room for second film title. The film title is large but cannot push all screening actions below the mobile opening viewport. Full-color art remains luminous, not purple-tinted; surrounding plum is the identity. Strict readable contrast and soft controlled transitions implied by stable layout.
